```plato

    //==
    // # ChiSquaredDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: DegreesOfFreedom (k), the number of squared standard
    // normals summed. Support is x > 0. Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chi-squared_distribution

    // The mean: the degrees of freedom.
    Mean(self: ChiSquaredDistribution): Number
        => self.DegreesOfFreedom;

    // The variance: twice the degrees of freedom.
    Variance(self: ChiSquaredDistribution): Number
        => 2.0 * self.DegreesOfFreedom;

    // The chi-squared density: x^(k/2-1) * exp(-x/2) / (2^(k/2) * Gamma(k/2))
    // for x > 0, zero at and below zero — the gamma density with shape k/2 and
    // scale 2.
    Pdf(self: ChiSquaredDistribution, value: Number): Number
    {
        var h = 0.5 * self.DegreesOfFreedom;
        return value <= 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : value.Pow(h - 1.0) * (-0.5 * value).Exp / (2.0.Pow(h) * Gamma(h));
    }

    // The chi-squared CDF: the regularized lower incomplete gamma P(k/2, x/2)
    // for x > 0, zero at and below zero.
    Cdf(self: ChiSquaredDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value <= 0.0
            ? 0.0
            : RegularizedGammaP(0.5 * self.DegreesOfFreedom, 0.5 * value);

    //==
    // # StudentTDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: DegreesOfFreedom (nu), location 0 and scale 1 (this is
    // the standard, non-shifted t). Support is the whole real line.
    // Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Student%27s_t-distribution

    // The mean: 0 by symmetry. Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 1 — the mean is
    // undefined at or below one degree of freedom, where this reports 0 anyway.
    Mean(self: StudentTDistribution): Number
        => 0.0;

    // The variance: nu / (nu - 2). Precondition: DegreesOfFreedom > 2; the
    // variance is infinite on (1, 2] and undefined at or below 1.
    Variance(self: StudentTDistribution): Number
        => self.DegreesOfFreedom / (self.DegreesOfFreedom - 2.0);

    // The Student-t density: (1 + t^2/nu)^(-(nu+1)/2) / (sqrt(nu) * B(1/2, nu/2)).
    Pdf(self: StudentTDistribution, value: Number): Number
    {
        var nu = self.DegreesOfFreedom;
        return (1.0 + value.Square / nu).Pow(-0.5 * (nu + 1.0))
             / (nu.Sqrt * Beta(0.5, 0.5 * nu));
    }

    // The Student-t CDF through the regularized incomplete beta: with
    // x = nu / (nu + t^2), the tail is I_x(nu/2, 1/2) / 2, so the CDF is the
    // tail for t < 0 and one minus the tail for t >= 0 (by the symmetry of the
    // density about 0; at t = 0 both branches give exactly 1/2).
    Cdf(self: StudentTDistribution, value: Number): Number
    {
        var nu = self.DegreesOfFreedom;
        var tail = 0.5 * RegularizedBeta(0.5 * nu, 0.5, nu / (nu + value.Square));
        return value < 0.0 ? tail : 1.0 - tail;
    }

    //==
    // # Heavy-tailed, lifetime, and shaped distribution bodies
    //
    // The `IProbabilityDistribution` obligations for the remaining continuous
    // families of `random.types.plato`: the heavy-tailed CauchyDistribution
    // and the peaked LaplaceDistribution, the lifetime and power-law
    // WeibullDistribution and ParetoDistribution, the bounded
    // TriangularDistribution, and the circular VonMisesDistribution. All bodies
    // here are exact closed forms except the von Mises CDF (which has no closed
    // form and is a truncated Bessel series; see its site); the Weibull moments
    // and the von Mises bodies go through `Gamma` and the modified Bessel
    // functions `BesselI0`/`BesselI1` of `numbers.library.plato`, so
    // their accuracy is bounded by the accuracy stated on those functions.

    //==
    // # CauchyDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: Location (x0, the median and mode) and Scale (gamma,
    // the half width at half maximum) — Scale is NOT a standard deviation; the
    // Cauchy distribution has none. Precondition: Scale > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauchy_distribution

    // The mean is undefined (the defining integral does not converge). By the
    // convention stated on the type, this reports the Location, which is the
    // median and mode.
    Mean(self: CauchyDistribution): Number
        => self.Location;

    // The variance is undefined. By the convention stated on the type, this
    // reports positive infinity, spelled as 1.0/0.0 — which is exactly the IEEE
    // +Infinity on every float backend, so it needs no constant. Deliberately
    // NOT adding a `PositiveInfinity` to `INumericalLimits`: that interface is
    // declared in the core/algebra interface files (owned elsewhere) and a new
    // member imposes a fresh obligation on every INumerical implementor
    // tree-wide, which is out of proportion to this one call.
    Variance(self: CauchyDistribution): Number
        => 1.0 / 0.0;

    // The Cauchy density: 1 / (pi * gamma * (1 + ((v - x0)/gamma)^2)). Exact.
    Pdf(self: CauchyDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => 1.0
         / (Number.Pi * self.Scale
            * (1.0 + ((value - self.Location) / self.Scale).Square));

    // The Cauchy CDF: 1/2 + atan((v - x0)/gamma) / pi. Exact. `Atan` returns an
    // `Angle` in this tree, so its Radians payload is taken explicitly.
    Cdf(self: CauchyDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => 0.5 + ((value - self.Location) / self.Scale).Atan.Radians / Number.Pi;

    //==
    // # LaplaceDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: Location (mu, the mean/median/mode) and Scale (b, the
    // "diversity") — the variance is 2b^2, so b is NOT a standard deviation.
    // Precondition: Scale > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laplace_distribution

    // The mean: the location parameter.
    Mean(self: LaplaceDistribution): Number
        => self.Location;

    // The variance: 2 * Scale^2.
    Variance(self: LaplaceDistribution): Number
        => 2.0 * self.Scale.Square;

    // The double-sided exponential density: exp(-|v - mu| / b) / (2b). Exact.
    Pdf(self: LaplaceDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => (-(value - self.Location).Abs / self.Scale).Exp / (2.0 * self.Scale);

    // The Laplace CDF: below the location, half the rising exponential; at or
    // above it, one minus half the falling exponential. Exact.
    Cdf(self: LaplaceDistribution, value: Number): Number
        => value < self.Location
            ? 0.5 * ((value - self.Location) / self.Scale).Exp
            : 1.0 - 0.5 * (-(value - self.Location) / self.Scale).Exp;

    //==
    // # WeibullDistribution
    //
    // Parameterization: SHAPE (k) and SCALE (lambda) — the two-parameter
    // Weibull with location 0, support x >= 0. Precondition: Shape > 0 and
    // Scale > 0.
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weibull_distribution

    // The mean: lambda * Gamma(1 + 1/k).
    Mean(self: WeibullDistribution): Number
        => self.Scale * Gamma(1.0 + 1.0 / self.Shape);
```
